object_description: ensemble of a multi-storey point structure and the flat volume of a ground-level hall
geometry_property: single-storey spatial layer along the streets
hall in the middle of the plot
design_condition: the ensemble occupies the plot with a point building and a low hall placed in the middle, bordered along the streets by a single-storey spatial layer, deliberately abandoning the diagonal grain of the quarter

positive: The scale of the surrounding area is well taken up
An independent presence and identity is sought for the rather introverted cultural centre
Widening the sidewalk creates some space for the typical local wooded edge
Equal accessibility of the hall from north and south shows a good analysis of the location and picks up the pedestrian flows from the village
The entrances behind palisades help minimise noise emissions from visitors before, during and after events
The gate facing the village centre signals the main entrance
The courtyards on both sides create a pleasant place to arrive and attractive outdoor spaces for outdoor events
The idea of maximum flexibility in the use of hall, foyer and outdoor spaces is consistently implemented
The approach continues into the ground floor multi-purpose room of the point building, which opens onto the courtyard
Sliding partition elements inside and outside make diverse use of space possible
The design is convincing in many respects and shows how a hall could become a hub of community life
negative: The authors deliberately abandon the characteristic diagonal building structure and green setbacks of the quarter
The open spaces created are too small to allow adequate greening
The gate gesture does not actually create an address
Outdoor events remain rather theoretical possibilities because of the protection of residents from emissions
The eastern private green space cannot create quality of stay, bounded by street space on two sides
The connection of side and rear rooms is not convincing with every seating option
Mobile room partitions require high-quality acoustic solutions and are maintenance-intensive
West-facing apartments are affected by emissions from the entrance courtyard of the hall below
Only two-thirds of the permitted use is utilised, which is likely to harm profitability
The project overshoots the mark and no longer meets the brief of the competition programme
